headline: Sellers Hold the Upper Hand as Friday's Session Turns Broadly Defensive
body_html:
Midday Friday finds the market firmly in retreat, with declining issues outnumbering advancers by more than two to one across the 519-name universe — 355 stocks lower against only 161 in the green. Homebuilders lead the damage, off more than two percent as a group, while Healthcare and Materials are each down sharply. The session's dominant theme is rotation away from rate-sensitive and economically exposed names, a posture amplified by geopolitical unease after President Trump convened his Cabinet at Camp David amid rising tensions with Iran.

Semiconductors are the lone sector in positive territory, nudging up 0.26%, a modest but meaningful distinction on an otherwise red tape. The standout mover by a wide margin is Roblox, cratering nearly thirty percent after results disappointed investors, dragging Internet-linked names lower. Infrastructure contractor MasTec is off more than eighteen percent, and Apple has shed close to ten percent, adding weight to the broad consumer-tech selloff.

Into the close, traders will be watching oil, which is pushing higher on shipping-flow concerns tied to drone activity near the Suez corridor. Energy is lower on the session despite firmer crude, suggesting margin anxiety rather than demand relief. Any escalation in Middle East headlines before the bell could deepen today's defensive tilt.

briefs.headline: SPX Technologies Surges on Earnings Beat, Leads Industrials Higher
briefs.body: SPX Technologies is up nearly sixteen percent midday Friday, by far the top gainer in the universe and the primary reason Industrials are clinging to flat on the session. The HVAC-focused manufacturer appears to have delivered results that cleared expectations by a meaningful margin, drawing fresh buying interest across the industrial complex.

briefs.headline: Roblox Plunge Drags Internet Gaming Peers Into the Red
briefs.body: Roblox is the session's most dramatic casualty, plummeting almost thirty percent and casting a shadow over the broader Internet-gaming category. The sharp selloff follows what the market is treating as a deeply disappointing earnings or guidance update, and the ripple effect is visible in related consumer-digital names heading into the afternoon.

briefs.headline: Drone Strike Near Suez Lifts Crude, Complicates Energy Sector Picture
briefs.body: Oil is gaining more than one percent midday after Egypt confirmed a drone struck two gas vessels at the Damietta port, stoking concern about export disruption along the Suez corridor. Despite firmer crude prices, Energy stocks remain in the red on the session, down 0.37%, as traders appear focused on downstream cost pressures rather than producer upside.

briefs.headline: MasTec Collapses Nearly Twenty Percent on Infrastructure Outlook Concerns
briefs.body: MasTec, the large infrastructure construction contractor, is among the session's worst performers with an eighteen-plus percent decline. The selloff suggests the market received forward guidance or project-update language that raised serious doubts about the near-term backlog, a worrying data point given broader infrastructure spending expectations tied to federal programs.

briefs.headline: IBM Chief Sets 2028–2029 as Quantum's Earnings Inflection Window
briefs.body: IBM's chief executive told investors that quantum computing is on track to deliver a measurable contribution to the company's financial results by 2028 or 2029. The comments provide one of the most concrete timelines yet offered by a major technology executive on the commercial readiness of quantum platforms, and are drawing attention in software and semiconductor circles.

briefs.headline: U.S. Cyber Agency Flags Escalating Threats to Water Infrastructure
briefs.body: The federal cybersecurity defense agency issued a warning Friday that malicious actors are intensifying attacks on water-treatment and distribution systems across the country. The alert arrives against a backdrop of broader infrastructure-security anxiety, including reports of surveillance activity linked to Iranian networks and the arrest of a suspected spy near a British military installation.
